finding: Seasonal margin collapse in Nov/Dec every year
measured_evidence: Nov/Dec avg profit margin 29.6% across all 5 years (range 29.1–30.2%). Baseline months (excl Jul/Nov/Dec) avg 46.4%. Nov/Dec avg order volume ~2763 vs typical ~1723 (+60%). 100% of Completed orders carry discount_amount > 0.
business_implication: A major annual promotional event drives 50-85% more orders at the cost of ~17pp of margin. Absolute profit is still higher in these months (~$1.0-1.2M vs ~$0.9-1.1M typical).
limitation: We cannot distinguish Black Friday/Cyber Monday from other promotions without campaign_name data (60% of Nov/Dec orders have null campaign_name). The multi-currency pool means absolute comparisons are imprecise.
recommended_action: Model the break-even discount threshold per currency. Test loyalty-member early-access at a smaller discount to recover 3-5pp margin. Add campaign_name capture to at least the top promotional events.

finding: July mid-year margin anomaly (~37-38%) without compensating volume
measured_evidence: July avg margin 38.0% across all 5 years (range 37.4–38.6%). July avg order volume 1683 vs typical 1723 — not materially higher. discount_amount is elevated in July rows.
business_implication: A mid-year promotional markdown is applied consistently without generating the volume uplift that would justify the margin sacrifice. Cost/benefit ratio is worse than the Nov/Dec event.
limitation: campaign_name is 60% null in July too; we cannot identify which specific promotion drives this. July pattern is consistent across all 5 years, suggesting a structural policy rather than a one-off event.
recommended_action: Audit the July discount policy. If it is a blanket platform-wide markdown, replace with targeted bundle deals or loyalty-point multipliers. Measure volume elasticity before the next July event.

finding: 75% of Completed orders concentrated in two channels (Mobile App + Website)
measured_evidence: Mobile App: 40.1% of Completed orders. Website: 34.9%. Combined: 74.9%. Profit margins are virtually identical across all four channels (~41.3-41.6%), so the concentration is purely in volume, not margin quality.
business_implication: Revenue is dependent on two platforms. A policy change, fee increase, or algorithm shift could materially impact revenue with no ready alternative. No margin incentive to stay in current mix.
limitation: Customer acquisition cost (CAC) per channel is not in this dataset. Without CAC, the true ROI of each channel cannot be computed; the lower-volume channels may still be cost-inefficient even if margins look equal.
recommended_action: Set a medium-term target to grow Marketplace + Social Media combined share. Append CAC data to future analyses to assess true channel ROI.

finding: On-time delivery rate 76.5% — systematically optimistic estimates
measured_evidence: On-time rate: 76.5% of 113,559 delivered orders (Completed + Returned with delivery data). Avg actual 4.56 days vs avg estimated 4.30 days (gap 0.26 days). Gap is consistent across all shipping methods (Same Day +0.33, Express +0.26, Standard +0.25, Economy +0.24).
business_implication: Customers are routinely receiving orders later than promised. This likely contributes to the 3.68/5 average rating and 30.5% Neutral sentiment.
limitation: delivery_status is null for 24,557 Cancelled/Pending orders — correctly excluded. We do not know whether 'Delayed' was communicated to customers in advance. Early deliveries (9,757 rows, 8.6%) offset some customer impact.
recommended_action: Add a 0.5-day buffer to customer-facing delivery estimates at zero operational cost. Audit warehouse throughput specifically in Nov/Dec when order volume peaks.

finding: Average customer rating 3.68/5 with 30.5% Neutral sentiment
measured_evidence: Mean rating 3.677/5.0 across 113,559 Completed orders (100% coverage). Distribution peaks at 3.6-3.8. Only 5.1% rate >=4.5. Sentiment: 68.8% Positive, 30.5% Neutral, 0.7% Negative.
business_implication: Customers are satisfied but not delighted. The large Neutral cluster has weak loyalty signal. Below typical industry benchmark of 4.2-4.5.
limitation: VIP customers rate highest (3.83) vs Business/Consumer (3.63). Rating data is available for Completed orders only — we cannot assess satisfaction for Cancelled or Pending customers, who may be more dissatisfied. The sentiment model may be loosely calibrated (68.8% Positive but mean only 3.68).
recommended_action: Cross-reference Neutral orders with delivery delay status. If delivery delay correlates, the delivery buffer fix (INS-04) has dual benefit. Consider post-delivery re-engagement nudge for 3.0-3.5 rated customers.

finding: Return rate 7.69% — uniform across regions and channels; root-cause data missing
measured_evidence: Return rate 7.69% (denominator: Completed+Returned). Range across regions: 7.19-7.99%. return_reason column is fully populated for all 9,462 Returned orders. Top reasons: Wrong Product (1,237), Other (1,208), Changed Mind (1,204), Size Issue (1,182), Defective Product (1,174), Late Delivery (1,172), Product Not as Expected (1,147), Damaged Product (1,138). Note: pandas reads the column as float64 on initial load due to 93% null across the full dataset; a str cast is required to read the text values.
business_implication: Uniform return rate across channels/regions suggests product-level driver. Root-cause analysis is now partially possible from return_reason values.
limitation: The original EDA script skipped return_reason breakdown due to float64 dtype. Now corrected: full text breakdown available in kpi_return_reasons.csv. Return rate is uniform across channels (7.19-7.79%) and regions (7.19-7.99%), suggesting product quality/expectation mismatch rather than channel or geography driver. No product/SKU dimension in dataset to drill further.
recommended_action: Return reasons are evenly distributed across 8 categories — no single dominant cause. Wrong Product (13.1%) + Defective Product (12.4%) + Damaged Product (12.0%) = 37.5% suggest operational/quality issues. Changed Mind (12.7%) + Product Not as Expected (12.1%) = 24.8% suggest product description gaps. Fix return_status/return_reason loading to use str cast in scripts. Focus product description improvements on top-volume items for expectation gap reductions.

finding: Loyalty redemption rate 49.9% — half of points unredeemed
measured_evidence: Total earned: 14,362,828  Total redeemed: 7,172,934  Rate: 49.9%. Avg earned/order: 126.5. Avg redeemed/order: 63.2.
business_implication: Half of earned loyalty value is unredeemed. Low redemption can reduce repeat purchase motivation. A redemption-drive campaign could pull forward purchases from existing customers at very low cost.
limitation: Point monetary value is not in this dataset — we cannot quantify the liability represented by unredeemed points or the actual discount a redemption campaign would cost. customer_order_count median is 7 (customers are already frequent), so repeat rate improvement from a nudge campaign may be modest.
recommended_action: Run a points-expiry reminder campaign for high-balance, low-recency customers. Quantify point monetary value from transaction data to size the liability and cost the campaign properly.

finding: 1,229 loss-making Completed orders (1.08%); 99.8% repeat rate is a row-level metric
measured_evidence: Loss-making Completed orders: 1,229 (1.08%). Total negative profit: -191,127.66. Min profit margin: -59.55%. Avg discount rate (loss orders): 51.72% vs 17.36% overall. CORRECTION: The 99.8% repeat customer rate is ORDER-ROW-LEVEL. Customer-level repeat rate = 98.66% (24,577 of 24,911 unique customers).
business_implication: 1.08% loss-making orders is small but indicates a pricing floor gap. The corrected customer-level repeat rate is still very high, confirming strong retention, but the 99.8% headline figure was misleading.
limitation: is_repeat_customer=False rows are each customer's FIRST order only. The column is consistent with the data but must not be used as a headline 'repeat customer rate' without the order-vs-customer distinction. Loss-making orders: without product/SKU data we cannot isolate specific loss-making product lines.
recommended_action: Update kpi_summary.csv to include customer_level_repeat_rate_%. Introduce a pricing floor rule: block checkout if computed profit < 0. Add SKU-level data to future datasets to isolate loss-making products.
